# CodesLytic Technologies — Full Site Content

> CodesLytic Technologies is an enterprise engineering and digital transformation partner. We design and build enterprise software, ERP platforms, web and mobile platforms, cloud infrastructure, data engineering pipelines, and AI/LLM integrations for manufacturing, finance, retail and technology businesses.

CodesLytic operates as an engineering partner, not a marketing agency: every engagement is scoped, architected and delivered by the team that maintains it in production.

#### PostgreSQL Database Administration & Optimization
URL: https://codeslytic.com/services/postgres-dba-optimization
Ongoing or specialized DBA engineering to guarantee high availability, performance, and stability.

We manage, optimize, and secure production PostgreSQL clustersfixing replication latency, optimizing slow queries, and architecting fault-tolerant database topologies for mission-critical applications.

Used by:
- High-traffic production applications facing database lock contention or query bottlenecks
- Enterprise systems requiring 24/7 uptime, automated backups, and HA streaming replication
- Companies seeking expert PostgreSQL DBA support without full-time in-house overhead

Process:
1. In-depth query plan analysis (EXPLAIN ANALYZE) and index structure optimization
2. Streaming replication setup, failover testing (Patroni / PgBouncer), and monitoring
3. Database parameter tuning (shared_buffers, work_mem, autovacuum parameters)
4. Comprehensive security, role-based access, and SSL/TLS encryption audit
5. Proactive health checks, lock escalation monitoring, and automated alert rules

Typical outcome: Sub-second query response times & 99.99% database uptime
Stack: PostgreSQL, PgBouncer, Patroni, Prometheus, Grafana, Linux

## Case Studies

### Enterprise Oracle → PostgreSQL Migration
URL: https://codeslytic.com/case-studies/oracle-to-postgresql-migration
Industry: Enterprise Finance & Core Systems. Category: Database Migration. Timeframe: 2025 - 2026.
Led zero-downtime migration of mission-critical Oracle databases to PostgreSQL, re-engineering complex PL/SQL stored procedures and cutting database licensing costs by 60%.

Impact metrics:
- Licensing Cost Savings: 60%. Reduction in annual database licensing and infrastructure spend
- Downtime During Cutover: 0 mins. Zero operational downtime achieved via parallel CDC replication
- Query Execution Speed: 3.5x. Average speedup across top 100 mission-critical database queries

Overview: A leading enterprise migrated its core relational database system from Oracle to open-source PostgreSQL to eliminate astronomical licensing fees while upgrading query performance for high-concurrency workloads.
Challenge: The legacy Oracle deployment relied heavily on deeply embedded PL/SQL packages, proprietary triggers, custom data types, and complex stored procedures. A naive migration risked broken application logic, data loss, and costly operational downtime during cutover.
Solution: Designed a multi-phase migration strategy featuring automated schema translation, manual PL/SQL to PL/pgSQL re-engineering, comprehensive unit testing, and parallel CDC (Change Data Capture) replication using AWS DMS to guarantee zero-downtime failover.

Architecture:
- Schema & Data Type Mapping: Converted Oracle specific types (NUMBER, VARCHAR2, CLOB) to native PostgreSQL types (NUMERIC, TEXT, JSONB).
- PL/SQL Re-Engineering: Translated 150+ PL/SQL procedures, packages, and triggers into optimized PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL functions.
- Zero-Downtime CDC Replication: Configured AWS DMS (Data Migration Service) for continuous data synchronization prior to cutover.
- Query & Index Tuning: Created targeted partial and GIN indexes and configured PgBouncer connection pooling for sub-millisecond query execution.

Results:
- Cut total database infrastructure & licensing costs by 60% annually.
- Executed 100% data-verified production cutover with zero downtime.
- Improved average transaction throughput by 35% under peak load.
- Eliminated vendor lock-in, enabling deployment across flexible cloud environments.

FAQs:
- Q: How was zero downtime achieved during the Oracle to PostgreSQL migration?
  A: Zero downtime was achieved by establishing continuous Change Data Capture (CDC) replication using AWS DMS between the live Oracle database and target PostgreSQL cluster. This allowed the application to cut over instantly with zero data loss or service interruption.
- Q: How were Oracle PL/SQL stored procedures converted to PostgreSQL?
  A: Legacy PL/SQL scripts were parsed and translated into PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL functions. Complex logic, autonomous transactions, and packages were modularized, refactored, and validated against an automated test suite to ensure exact behavioral parity.
- Q: What financial impact did this database migration deliver?
  A: The migration achieved a 60% reduction in annual database licensing and cloud infrastructure spend, paying back the project investment within 6 months.

Stack: Oracle, PostgreSQL, PL/SQL, PL/pgSQL, AWS DMS, PgBouncer, Python

### Cross-Region Data Lake Migration & Airflow Automation
URL: https://codeslytic.com/case-studies/cross-region-data-lake-migration
Industry: Global Logistics & Analytics. Category: Data Lake Engineering. Timeframe: 2023 - 2024.
Migrated a full enterprise data lake ecosystem across AWS cloud regions while implementing Apache Airflow orchestration, boosting pipeline turnaround efficiency by 50%.

Impact metrics:
- Pipeline Turnaround: +50%. Improvement in data processing speed and workflow turnaround time
- Data Volume Migrated: 500+ TB. Seamless multi-region object storage and catalog transfer with zero loss
- Automated Workflows: 200+ DAGs. Production Apache Airflow DAGs orchestrating continuous data ingestion

Overview: Migrated a multi-terabyte data lake ecosystem across cloud regions to optimize regional latency and compliance while replacing legacy cron/shell data scripts with automated Apache Airflow pipelines.
Challenge: The existing data lake spanned hundreds of terabytes in AWS S3 and Hadoop, with fragmented ingestion scripts causing frequent pipeline failures, delayed reporting, and high cross-region data transfer costs.
Solution: Architected a cross-region migration plan leveraging AWS S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) and AWS Lake Formation, paired with a complete modernization of ETL pipelines into containerized Apache Airflow DAGs with concurrent data refresh logic.

Architecture:
- Cross-Region Transfer: Synchronized S3 buckets across regions with bandwidth control and checksum validation.
- Airflow Pipeline Modernization: Re-engineered legacy shell and Python scripts into modular Apache Airflow DAGs.
- Concurrent Refresh Architecture: Implemented parallelized Spark batch jobs to update data lake partitions simultaneously.
- Data Governance: Set up AWS Lake Formation for centralized access policy control and catalog management.

Results:
- Improved overall pipeline execution and data turnaround efficiency by 50%.
- Reduced cross-region bandwidth overhead and cloud storage spend.
- Achieved automated failure recovery, SLA tracking, and instant alerts for data operators.
- Guaranteed compliance with multi-region data residency requirements.

FAQs:
- Q: How did Apache Airflow improve pipeline turnaround efficiency by 50%?
  A: Apache Airflow replaced sequential, unmonitored cron jobs with dynamically orchestrated DAGs that run independent tasks concurrently, handle intelligent retries, and eliminate idle wait states between data dependencies.
- Q: How was data integrity verified during the cross-region data lake migration?
  A: Automated validation scripts computed cryptographic MD5/SHA-256 checksums and row counts across source and destination S3 partitions prior to switching active ingestion endpoints.

Stack: Apache Airflow, AWS S3, Hadoop, PySpark, AWS Glue, AWS Lake Formation, Python

### Greenfield AWS Redshift Data Warehouse Build
URL: https://codeslytic.com/case-studies/aws-data-warehouse-build
Industry: Enterprise Business Intelligence. Category: Data Warehousing. Timeframe: 2021 - 2023.
Designed and built an enterprise AWS Redshift Data Warehouse from scratch, unifying disparate data streams into sub-second BI reporting dashboards.

Impact metrics:
- Data Source Integration: 100%. Unification of disparate ERP, CRM, and transactional SQL data sources
- Query Execution Speed: <1 sec. Sub-second response time for complex executive BI queries
- Reporting Automated: 24/7. Continuous, automated data refresh for executive decision making

Overview: Built the organization's foundational cloud data warehouse on AWS Redshift, consolidating isolated data silos across ERPs, CRMs, and operational databases into a single, unified reporting platform.
Challenge: Business leaders lacked a single source of truth; operational data was scattered across legacy databases, flat files, and third-party SaaS APIs, requiring manual spreadsheet consolidation that took days.
Solution: Architected a modern AWS data lakehouse architectureusing PySpark and Apache Sqoop to ingest raw data into an S3 Data Lake, transformed via dbt/Airflow into dimensional star-schema data marts inside AWS Redshift.

Architecture:
- Ingestion Engine: Deployed PySpark and Sqoop jobs for high-throughput batch and incremental database extraction.
- S3 Staging Lake: Established raw, cleaned, and curated S3 storage layers with Parquet columnar compression.
- Redshift Data Marts: Modeled dimensional Fact and Dimension tables optimized with sort and distribution keys.
- BI Integration: Connected AWS QuickSight and Power BI directly to Redshift for real-time executive reporting.

Results:
- Eliminated 100% of manual spreadsheet reporting efforts across finance and operations.
- Delivered sub-second query response times for executive dashboards.
- Created a central data governance model with role-based access security.
- Enabled self-serve data analytics for business analysts across departments.

FAQs:
- Q: Why was AWS Redshift chosen for this greenfield data warehouse?
  A: AWS Redshift was selected for its native integration with AWS S3, Redshift Spectrum capability for querying raw data lake files directly, exceptional petabyte-scale query performance, and cost-effective RA3 node scaling.
- Q: How were disparate data sources unified into the data warehouse?
  A: Automated ingestion scripts using PySpark and Apache Sqoop extracted schema data from relational databases and SaaS APIs into S3. Airflow DAGs then cleaned, normalized, and transformed the data into dimensional data marts inside Redshift.

Stack: AWS Redshift, AWS S3, PySpark, Apache Sqoop, AWS Glue, Apache Airflow, QuickSight

### Azure to AWS Data Warehouse & Pipeline Migration
URL: https://codeslytic.com/case-studies/azure-to-aws-migration
Industry: Multi-Cloud Enterprise. Category: Cloud Migration. Timeframe: 2021.
Migrated Azure Synapse and Data Factory workloads to AWS Redshift and Apache Airflow, cutting compute spend by 25% while expanding processing capacity.

Impact metrics:
- Compute Cost Cut: 25%. Direct savings on monthly cloud data warehousing compute expenses
- Migration Cutover Time: 1 Weekend. Flawless cutover with zero interruption to Monday morning operations
- Pipeline Reliability: 99.9%. SLA compliance for daily executive reporting deliverables

Overview: Executed a complete cross-cloud migration of enterprise data warehouse workloads from Microsoft Azure Synapse and Azure Data Factory to AWS Redshift and Apache Airflow.
Challenge: High and unpredictable Azure Synapse compute licensing fees, paired with complex cross-cloud architecture, slowed down query performance and escalated IT operational budgets.
Solution: Converted T-SQL scripts to Redshift PostgreSQL-compliant SQL, translated Azure Data Factory pipelines into Python-native Airflow DAGs, and migrated historical data directly to AWS S3 and Redshift.

Architecture:
- Code Translation: Converted Azure Synapse T-SQL stored procedures and views to AWS Redshift SQL.
- Pipeline Modernization: Replaced Azure Data Factory pipelines with open-source Apache Airflow DAGs.
- Data Transfer: Leveraged encrypted AWS Snowball / multi-part S3 upload for secure cross-cloud data transfer.
- Cost Optimization: Configured AWS Redshift pause/resume and concurrency scaling to minimize idle compute fees.

Results:
- Reduced monthly cloud data warehousing compute spend by 25%.
- Accelerated batch processing execution by 30%.
- Streamlined operations by standardizing infrastructure on AWS.
- Eliminated proprietary vendor lock-in by using open Airflow DAGs.

FAQs:
- Q: How was a 25% reduction in compute costs achieved during the Azure to AWS migration?
  A: The 25% cost reduction was achieved by moving from Azure Synapse DWUs to AWS Redshift RA3 instances with decoupled compute and storage, alongside right-sizing node clusters and replacing proprietary Azure Data Factory fees with open-source Apache Airflow.
- Q: Were T-SQL scripts fully compatible with AWS Redshift?
  A: No, Azure Synapse T-SQL scripts required conversion for Redshift's PostgreSQL-based syntax. Functions, data types, and stored procedure logic were refactored and validated prior to deployment.

Stack: AWS Redshift, Azure Synapse, Apache Airflow, Python, SQL, AWS S3

### ERP & CRM Manufacturing Platform
URL: https://codeslytic.com/case-studies/erp-crm-platform
Industry: Manufacturing & Operations. Category: Enterprise Software. Timeframe: 2024.
Unified ERP and CRM platform covering production planning, inventory tracking, BOM workflows, and legacy system modernization.

Impact metrics:
- Inventory Accuracy: 99.8%. Real-time ledger tracking across raw materials and finished goods
- BOM Processing Speed: 5x. Faster creation and job-card assignment for production runs
- Paperwork Eliminated: 100%. Digital shop-floor logging replacing paper job cards

Overview: Implemented a custom ERP and CRM platform based on Frappe and Next.js for a multi-facility manufacturing company, replacing manual paper logs with real-time digital tracking.
Challenge: The manufacturing client suffered from stock discrepancies, delayed job orders, and fragmented customer communications due to separate legacy accounting and warehouse spreadsheets.
Solution: Customized CodesLytic ERP modules for Bill of Materials (BOM), work orders, purchasing, and stock entry, paired with a custom Next.js portal for customer order tracking and CRM management.

Architecture:
- BOM Engine: Configured multi-level Bill of Materials with automated scrap loss calculations.
- Stock Ledger Integration: Real-time FIFO inventory valuation across multiple plant warehouses.
- Custom Next.js Frontend: Responsive web portal for sales reps and customers to place and track custom orders.
- Role-Based Access: Fine-grained security profiles for shop-floor operators, warehouse staff, and executives.

Results:
- Achieved 99.8% inventory ledger accuracy across all facilities.
- Reduced order-to-production turnaround time by 60%.
- Streamlined procurement with automated reorder level alerts.
- Provided leadership with real-time gross margin analytics per production run.

FAQs:
- Q: How did the ERP platform improve manufacturing productivity?
  A: By digitizing Bill of Materials (BOM) creation and job card generation, production teams eliminated manual data entry errors and gained instant visibility into material availability before starting a run.
- Q: Is Frappe/CodesLytic ERP customizable for specific factory workflows?
  A: Yes, Frappe's Python/MariaDB architecture allows full custom doctype development, automated workflow hooks, and custom React/Next.js frontend integrations tailored to exact shop-floor processes.

### Token Launchpad Platform
URL: https://codeslytic.com/case-studies/token-launchpad-platform
Industry: Blockchain & Web3. Category: FinTech. Timeframe: 2023 - 2024.
Developed an enterprise web3 launchpad supporting automated token sales, KYC investor onboarding, and multi-wallet integrations.

Impact metrics:
- Transaction Volume: $10M+. Total token sale value processed through smart contract logic
- Wallet Support: 10+ Wallets. Seamless Wagmi/RainbowKit integration across major crypto wallets
- Security Audits: 100% Clean. Zero vulnerabilities detected in production smart contract audits

Overview: Built a secure, high-concurrency web3 token launchpad platform enabling crypto projects to conduct verified public and private token generation events.
Challenge: Existing launchpad solutions lacked enterprise-grade KYC/AML compliance, suffered from RPC node connection timeouts during high-traffic token sales, and had complex UI friction.
Solution: Architected a Next.js web application integrated with Wagmi, Ethers.js, automated SumSub KYC verification, and redundant RPC provider fallback clusters.

Architecture:
- Web3 Frontend: React/Next.js interface with stateful wallet session persistence.
- Multi-RPC Fallback: Connected Alchemy, QuickNode, and Infura fallback nodes for zero-downtime minting.
- KYC/AML Automation: Integrated API hooks for instant investor identity verification.
- Smart Contract Hooks: Event listeners tracking token allocations, vesting schedules, and claims.

Results:
- Processed over $10M in token sales across multiple high-traffic launch events.
- Handled over 50,000 concurrent wallet connections without downtime.
- Achieved 100% compliance with international investor onboarding regulations.
- Reduced user transaction failure rates to under 0.01%.

FAQs:
- Q: How were RPC node failures prevented during gas wars?
  A: We implemented an RPC provider failover array using Wagmi fallback providers, automatically routing traffic to secondary nodes if primary latency exceeded 500ms.
- Q: How is investor KYC handled on-chain?
  A: KYC verification is completed off-chain via automated identity APIs, which issue cryptographically signed attestations that investors submit when calling smart contract buy functions.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, Wagmi, Ethers.js, Tailwind CSS, Node.js

### Automated Cloud Infrastructure Platform
URL: https://codeslytic.com/case-studies/cloud-infrastructure-platform
Industry: Technology & SaaS. Category: Cloud Engineering. Timeframe: 2023 - 2024.
Containerized enterprise workloads with automated IaC Terraform deployment pipelines and 24x7 Prometheus/Grafana monitoring.

Impact metrics:
- Infrastructure Uptime: 99.99%. Guaranteed SLA uptime across containerized production microservices
- Deployment Speed: 10 mins. Automated CI/CD pipeline code push to production staging
- Cloud Cost Savings: 30%. Reduction in monthly AWS compute spend via spot instance orchestration

Overview: Migrated a scaling SaaS platform from manual EC2 deployments to an automated, containerized AWS EKS (Kubernetes) infrastructure managed with Terraform.
Challenge: Manual server provisioning led to configuration drift, deployment outages, slow developer onboarding, and high idle cloud infrastructure expenses.
Solution: Architected declarative Infrastructure as Code using Terraform, containerized microservices with Docker, deployed to AWS EKS, and built automated GitHub Actions CI/CD pipelines.

Architecture:
- Terraform IaC: Modular infrastructure code defining VPCs, subnets, EKS clusters, and IAM roles.
- Kubernetes Deployment: EKS cluster with HPA (Horizontal Pod Autoscaler) and cluster autoscaling.
- CI/CD Pipeline: GitHub Actions workflows with automated container image scanning and canary deployments.
- Observability Stack: Prometheus metric collection paired with custom Grafana alert dashboards.

Results:
- Achieved 99.99% operational uptime across all production web services.
- Reduced release deployment times from 2 hours to under 10 minutes.
- Cut monthly AWS cloud spend by 30% using EC2 spot instance node groups.
- Eliminated configuration drift across development, staging, and production environments.

FAQs:
- Q: How does cluster autoscaling optimize cloud costs?
  A: AWS EKS cluster autoscaler adjusts the number of EC2 worker nodes dynamically based on active pod resource requests, scaling down idle nodes during off-peak hours.
- Q: How are production deployments protected against broken builds?
  A: CI/CD pipelines enforce automated linting, unit test coverage minimums, image security scanning, and canary deployment rollouts with instant automated rollbacks on error.

Stack: AWS, Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes, EKS, GitHub Actions, Prometheus, Grafana

### Cross-Chain NFT Marketplace
URL: https://codeslytic.com/case-studies/cross-chain-nft-marketplace
Industry: Blockchain. Category: Web3. Timeframe: 2022 - 2023.
Multi-chain marketplace featuring non-custodial wallet authentication, gas-optimized smart contract interaction, and high-speed asset indexing.

Impact metrics:
- Indexing Speed: <500ms. Real-time block indexing for new mints and token transfers
- Chains Supported: Ethereum & Polygon. Cross-chain asset browsing and checkout integration
- Platform Uptime: 99.95%. Continuous marketplace availability during high-demand mints

Overview: Engineered a high-speed cross-chain digital asset marketplace allowing users to trade, list, and auction NFTs across Ethereum and Polygon networks.
Challenge: Public blockchain indexing APIs suffered from rate limits and high latency, causing stale marketplace listings and failed transaction confirmations during peak minting events.
Solution: Built a custom Node.js and MongoDB block indexing engine that listens to EVM WebSocket events, paired with a lightweight React frontend.

Architecture:
- Custom EVM Indexer: Node.js worker threads consuming EVM logs to maintain low-latency asset state.
- MongoDB Metadata Store: High-throughput document store caching NFT attributes, ownership, and sales history.
- Web3 Wallet Integration: Support for MetaMask, WalletConnect, and Coinbase Wallet.
- Gas Optimization: Optimized smart contract interaction logic to minimize gas overhead for buyers.

Results:
- Delivered sub-500ms metadata updates upon block confirmation.
- Handled over 100,000 active user listings with zero indexer lag.
- Reduced buyer gas fee overhead by 22% through batch contract calls.
- Maintained 99.95% platform availability during major collection launches.

FAQs:
- Q: How does the custom block indexer handle blockchain reorgs?
  A: The indexer maintains a 20-block rolling history buffer and automatically rolls back and re-indexes database state if a block reorganization is detected on-chain.
- Q: How are IPFS metadata files cached for fast loading?
  A: Original IPFS asset metadata and media are ingested, compressed, and served through a global CDN edge caching layer.

Stack: React, Web3.js, Node.js, MongoDB, Express, IPFS, Tailwind CSS

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How is CodesLytic different from legacy IT giants like TCS or Wipro?
Legacy IT giants suffer from heavy administrative bloat, slow account management bureaucracy, high pricing markups, and junior developers assigned behind sales decks. CodesLytic is a specialized, hands-on engineering squad. You communicate directly with senior developers and data engineers who audit, build, and deploy your codebase  delivering enterprise quality faster and far more cost-effectively.

### Can you execute Oracle to PostgreSQL database migrations without downtime?
Yes. We utilize continuous Change Data Capture (CDC) replication via AWS DMS paired with manual PL/SQL to PL/pgSQL logic re-engineering. The target PostgreSQL cluster remains synchronized in real time while application logic is verified, enabling an instantaneous cutover window with zero data loss.

### What is your project engagement model and pricing structure?
We offer transparent fixed-scope milestone projects or sprint-based dedicated engineering retainers. Because we operate without corporate administrative bloat, our pricing is typically 40-50% more cost-effective than traditional agencies while giving you direct senior engineer access.

### How quickly can CodesLytic start on an architecture audit or build?
We schedule an initial technical discovery call within 24-48 hours. After evaluating your codebase, database schema, or operational requirements, we deliver a technical assessment, execution plan, and timeline within 3-5 business days.

### Can you embed with our existing internal engineering team?
Absolutely. We frequently collaborate with in-house engineering teams as dedicated domain specialists  executing complex database migrations, building greenfield AWS Redshift warehouses, deploying RAG AI pipelines, or accelerating web/mobile platform releases.
